If you've been bracing for a layoff wave, the latest data points the other way.

U.S. employers announced 43,994 job cuts in October — the fewest for any month since 2023. A year ago, October 2025 set a 22-year high at 153,074 cuts, so this October is down about 71%. At the same time, employers announced plans to hire 444,692 workers in October, the most for the month since 2009 (Challenger, Gray & Christmas, Nov. 5).

It's your paycheck: fewer cuts and more hiring plans is a steadier job market than the AI-layoff headlines suggest — though economists still call it a low-fire, low-hire market.

My take: read the data, not the fear. The scary headline isn't always the real one.
